title: A best-effort clear of a handover record gives no adversary in the threat model anything beyond what an already-documented exposure window provides
component: encrypted data-volume ownership handover record clearing
claim: A candidate found that clearing a one-time ownership-handover record after a successful handover is best-effort: if the clearing write itself fails, the record can persist past the single boot the project's own documentation says it lasts, widening a documented exposure window.
location: encrypted data-volume handover record clearing and reopening code; related documentation
why_not_a_finding: The code behavior is exactly as the candidate describes, and the documentation's wording is narrower than the code's actual behavior, which is a residual documentation point kept separately. As a security candidate it does not hold: no ordinary boot path can trigger the failing write with no fault present, no reachable code path lets a sandboxed process trigger the failure, and the one adversary who could benefit from a stretched window already has, by the project's own threat model and its own documentation, everything they would gain from a forced failure the moment they have physical access to the storage during that window.
routes_tried: Checked whether an ordinary boot that does not persist state can trigger the failing write with no attacker present: it cannot, because the volume in question is never opened at all on such a boot.
Checked whether a sandboxed process could cause the clearing write to fail: the write goes through the kernel's own block-device layer outside any sandboxed process's reach on every path examined.

Checked what the adversary who already has physical access during the documented window could gain from a forced write failure: nothing beyond what that same access already gives them, which the project's own documentation already states explicitly.
Identified the documentation wording gap directly and recorded it separately as a non-security residual.

steps: Independently re-derived the control flow from the relevant source files rather than relying on the original write-up's line references, which had drifted from the current commit.
No fault-injected disk test or booted-kernel test was performed; this was a code-reading review.
